title: Choosing the right doctor or primary care provider
summary: Explains why to have a primary care provider, types of primary care providers, how to choose a doctor and where to find mental health, vision and dental providers.

atoms.title: Network providers lower costs
atoms.question: Why should I choose a network provider?
atoms.text: Choosing a network provider may help lower costs. Most plans charge more if you see an out-of-network provider, and some will not cover out-of-network care at all. To see if a primary care provider is in your network, view UnitedHealthcare network providers in your member account or browse a provider list.
questions: How do I check if a doctor is in network?

atoms.title: Why you need a primary care provider
atoms.question: Why do I need a primary care provider?
atoms.text: Some health plans require you to choose a primary care provider (PCP), and while others do not, it may be a good idea to have one. A PCP can guide you through your care and, as they get to know you, may watch for small changes in your health to help spot warning signs of potential health concerns earlier. Your PCP may also save you money with fewer ER visits, can connect you with specialists and can advocate for you.
questions: What does a primary care provider do?

atoms.title: Seeing a specialist without a referral
atoms.question: Can I see a specialist without a referral?
atoms.text: Whether you need a referral often depends on your health plan and the specialist's office. With certain plans you can make appointments with a specialist on your own, while other plans may need a referral from a PCP before the visit is covered. If you are not sure, check your plan details or call the specialist's office before you schedule.
questions: Do I need a referral to see a specialist?
How do I know if my plan requires referrals?

atoms.title: Types of primary care providers
atoms.question: What types of primary care providers are there?
atoms.text: Each family member may need a different PCP. A family medicine doctor provides preventive and whole-person care for patients of all ages. An OB/GYN specializes in women's health, including family planning, pregnancy and menopause. A pediatrician serves patients from newborn to 18 years old. An internist treats adults 18 and older. A geriatrician focuses on medical conditions related to aging in older adults aged 60 and up.
questions: What is the difference between a family doctor and an internist?

atoms.title: Board certification
atoms.question: How can I check whether a doctor is board certified?
atoms.text: Board certification is a sign of going above and beyond state licensing requirements and receiving supervised in-practice training. To find a board-certified family doctor, you can visit the American Board of Family Medicine online directory, and to check whether a physician is board-certified you can use the American Board of Medical Specialties' Certification Matters database.
questions: How do I verify a doctor's credentials?

atoms.title: Mental and behavioral health provider types
atoms.question: What kinds of mental health providers are there?
atoms.text: Many types of providers can support your mental health, and some people benefit from seeing a combination of mental health professionals. These may include social workers, counselors or therapists, psychiatrists and psychologists. UnitedHealthcare offers a separate guide to choosing a mental health provider.
questions: What is the difference between a psychologist and a psychiatrist?
Who should I see for mental health?

atoms.title: Vision care and dental providers
atoms.question: What eye care and dental providers can I choose?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare Vision network includes two types of eye care providers, optometrists and ophthalmologists, and UnitedHealthcare encourages visiting the eye doctor even if you do not wear glasses or contacts. Routine dental care is important to overall health, and a plan may include coverage for cleanings, fluoride, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions and dentures.
questions: What is the difference between an optometrist and ophthalmologist?
Does my plan cover dental cleanings?

atoms.title: Questions to ask when choosing a doctor
atoms.question: How do I choose a doctor?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare suggests researching before choosing a doctor. Questions include whether friends, family, specialists or other health professionals recommend them, why people like this doctor, whether gender or age matters, whether you prefer a clinic close to home or work, how far you are willing to drive, and how their consumer reviews look. Reviews are just opinions, so one or two may not paint the whole picture.
questions: How do I pick a good primary care doctor?
Should I trust online doctor reviews?

atoms.title: Consider virtual visits
atoms.question: Can I see a provider virtually instead of in person?
atoms.text: Virtual visits, also known as telehealth, let you connect with a health care provider using your computer, tablet or smartphone and may be covered by your health plan just like an office visit. Depending on your benefits, you may be able to schedule a virtual visit with a local provider and book virtual visits for primary care, therapy, specialty care or urgent care when your provider is not available.
